key_insight: An AI fiber-orientation surrogate became a usable crash CAE tool by integrating gate-setting support, automatic mapping, and reporting into one GUI.
engineering_relevance: Crash CAE engineers can prepare orientation fields without molding-specialist support in about 0.1 hours instead of 25 hours—a 99.6% reduction.
method: Support injection-gate estimation when gate locations are unknown.
Voxelize geometry, infer fiber orientation, and automatically map it to the crash CAE model.
Generate shareable reports within a unified GUI.
evidence_signal: Validation progressed from 2D plates to production parts against a predefined angular-error criterion; component crash analysis reduced absolute peak-force error from 19.0% with an isotropic baseline to 11.4% and confined predicted fracture to the test-observed region.
watch_item: Deployment remains initial and limited to directed fracture-prediction scenarios; broader applicability is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
